EMPIRICAL RESEARCH PLAN  

================================================================  
1. IDENTIFICATION STRATEGY  
----------------------------------------------------------------  
Main strategy:  
A. Classical market-model EVENT STUDY around each of the three media events to isolate cumulative abnormal returns (CARs) and abnormal volumes (AVOL).  
B. Difference-in-Differences (DiD) panel regression to estimate the incremental effect of the May-3-1998 “mega-publicity” shock on ENMD and on spill-over firms relative to suitable controls.

Why appropriate?  
• Event study: the attention shocks are sharp, externally‐timed, and we have minute- and day-level data ⇒ standard in the asset-pricing literature.  
• DiD: lets us quantify whether the post-event drift (or reversal) for treated stocks differs from parallel firms that were not highlighted, controlling for common market movements and firm fixed effects.  
Combining the two allows us to speak to both “instantaneous” mispricing and longer-run permanence.  

================================================================  
2. TREATMENT AND CONTROL  
----------------------------------------------------------------  
A. Direct-effect sample (EntreMed)  
   • Treatment variable Treated_i = 1 if firm == “ENMD”, 0 otherwise.  
   • Control group: 134 Nasdaq Combined Biotech Index constituents EXCLUDING ENMD.  
   • Event date t₀ = Monday, 4-May-1998 (first trading day after NYT front-page story).  
   • Event window for DiD: 10 trading days PRE (-10 to ‑1) and 40 trading days POST (0 to +40).  
B. Spill-over sample  
   • Treated_i = 1 if firm is a cancer/angiogenesis biotech (identified via textual screening of 10-K and S-1 filings) OR if it is in the Nasdaq Biotech Index (“close industry peers”).  
   • Control group: (i) non-cancer biotech firms of similar size, and (ii) synthetic match of Russell 2000 non-biotech stocks.  
   • Same timing as above.  

We will repeat the design for the November-27-1997 “scientific” article (new information) and the November-12-1998 “negative replication” article (negative attention) to compare reactions to (a) new fundamentals, (b) recycled publicity, and (c) negative publicity.

No RDD or IV is needed; the sharp timing provides the quasi-experiment.  

================================================================  
3. KEY IDENTIFYING ASSUMPTIONS  
----------------------------------------------------------------  
A1. Parallel trends (DiD): Abnormal returns of treated and control firms would have evolved similarly absent the publicity shock.  
Plausibility: Both sets operate in the same trading environment; a 10-day pre-period will be plotted to verify.  

A2. No other simultaneous firm-specific news for ENMD or the peer group.  
Plausibility: SEC filings and news wires will be screened; none are recorded for 4-May-1998.  

A3. Market model is correctly specified in the estimation window (for CARs).  
Plausibility: Standard 120-day estimation window (-140,-21 days) is customary; robustness will use Fama-French factors.  

A4. No anticipation/insider leakage before the NYT Sunday article.  
Plausibility: We will inspect intraday TAQ on Fri 1-May-1998; volume spike absence would support this.  

================================================================  
4. THREATS TO IDENTIFICATION & MITIGATION  
----------------------------------------------------------------  
T1. Confounding macro or industry news (e.g., FDA guidance) on 4-May-1998.  
   → Search Dow Jones, Bloomberg, LexisNexis; include daily industry-level fixed effect; run placebo on non-biotech firms.  

T2. ENMD’s extremely small float could yield price pressure unrelated to attention.  
   → Use volume-weighted returns; check bid-ask bounce; replicate analysis with quote-midpoints and with equal-weighted vs value-weighted returns.  

T3. Selection of peer firms (spill-over analysis).  
   → Propensity-score match on size, cash, beta, and prior volatility; show results for three alternative control constructions.  

================================================================  
5. R CODE OUTLINE  
----------------------------------------------------------------  
```r
# 0. Packages
library(data.table)
library(lubridate)
library(fixest)
library(xts)
library(PerformanceAnalytics)

# 1. Load data (assumes three csv files)
prices  <- fread("daily_prices.csv")    # firm, date, price, volume
market  <- fread("market_factors.csv")  # date, mkt_rf, smb, hml, rf
mapping <- fread("firm_characteristics.csv") # firm, treated, cancer_peer, float

# 2. Merge & clean
prices[, date := ymd(date)]
setkeyv(prices, c("firm","date"))
dat <- merge(prices, mapping, by = "firm", all.x = TRUE)
dat <- merge(dat, market, by = "date",  all.x = TRUE)

# 3. Return calculations
setorder(dat, firm, date)
dat[, ret := (shift(price, type = "lead") - price)/price , by = firm]   
dat[, excess_ret := ret - rf]

# 4. Abnormal returns using market model over (-140,-21)
event_day <- ymd("1998-05-04")
est_window <- dat[date %between% c(event_day-140, event_day-21)]

# estimate betas
betas <- est_window[ , .(alpha = coef(lm(excess_ret ~ mkt_rf))[1],
                         beta  = coef(lm(excess_ret ~ mkt_rf))[2]),
                     by = firm]

# merge betas and compute abnormal
dat <- merge(dat, betas, by="firm", all.x=TRUE)
dat[, abret := excess_ret - (alpha + beta*mkt_rf)]

# 5. Construct DiD variables
dat[, post := as.integer(date >= event_day)]
dat[, window := as.integer(date >= event_day-10 & date <= event_day+40)]
panel <- dat[window==1]          # keep analysis window
panel[, treat_ENMD := (firm=="ENMD")]
panel[, treat_peer := cancer_peer]

# 6. Main DiD regression: ENMD vs other biotech
reg1 <- feols(abret ~ treat_ENMD*post | firm + date, data = panel, se = "hetero")
summary(reg1)

# 7. Dynamic event-study (optional)
panel[, rel_day := as.integer(date - event_day)]
for (k in -10:40) panel[, paste0("D",k) := (rel_day==k)]
dyn_formula <- as.formula(
  paste("abret ~ ", paste(paste0("D", -10:40, "*treat_ENMD"), collapse="+"),
        "| firm + date"))
reg_dyn <- feols(dyn_formula, data = panel, se="hetero")

# 8. Spill-over DiD
panel[, treat_spill := treat_peer]
reg2 <- feols(abret ~ treat_spill*post | firm + date, data = panel, se = "hetero")

# 9. Robustness: placebo event 4-May-1997
placebo_day <- ymd("1997-05-05")
panel_pbo <- dat[date %between% c(placebo_day-10, placebo_day+40)]
panel_pbo[, post := (date>=placebo_day)]
panel_pbo[, treat_ENMD := (firm=="ENMD")]
reg_pbo <- feols(abret ~ treat_ENMD*post | firm + date, data=panel_pbo, se="hetero")
summary(reg_pbo)
```

================================================================  
6. EXPECTED RESULTS  
----------------------------------------------------------------  
• ENMD: one-day CAR ≈ +300% to +400% (historically it quadrupled).  
• Longer-horizon (0,+40) CAR expected to partially mean-revert but remain >0, maybe +150%.  
• Spill-over firms: day-0 CAR of +3% to +6%; likely to dissipate within a month.  
• Volume: 10-to-20× normal on event day; elevated for a week.  
These magnitudes follow attention/limits-to-arbitrage theories (Barberis et al., 1998).  

================================================================  
7. VALIDITY CHECKLIST SELF-ASSESSMENT (DiD)  
----------------------------------------------------------------  
C1: Pre-trends visually parallel  → 1  
C2: No contemporaneous confounders  → 0.8 (some residual risk)  
C3: No anticipation  → 0.7  
C4: Stable composition of treatment & control groups  → 1  
C5: SUTVA (no interference beyond spill-over definition)  → 0.6  
Overall ≈ 4.1 / 5  

================================================================  
End of plan.
